Investor view · private

What NASHA is, and what is actually proven.

Concept stage Not public Not an offer

NASHA is a concept for food and beer designed together, joining Indian and Mexican traditions, in Austin, Texas. This page is a private, unindexed concept view. It is not an offer, it does not ask for money, and no investor has been approached. Everything is labelled by how much is real.

The pre-capital phase is being used to remove as much uncertainty as possible before anyone is asked to fund expensive uncertainty: what can be written down and designed with time and research is being documented; what can be tested personally will be tested; what needs money is named, with what each category would unlock.

The project's own readiness record shows physical evidence at 4 of 95 and design at 43 of 95. Design is not proof. Digital work never raises the evidence number.

Why this, and why a brewery

  • Why India and Mexico: Founder thesis, untested: two traditions that already share heat, acid, corn-and-fry technique and a fondness for sharing plates can be joined into dishes that feel like one cuisine, not two. Cultural advisor review is pending.
  • Why food and beer together: Founder thesis, untested: designing beer and food together makes pairing a reason to visit. Our own analysis says a host-brewery or collaboration path could test this with far less capital than a brewery.
  • Why a brewery at all: Untested. The brewery is the LAST capital gate, after food, demand and economics are shown.
  • Why Austin: Founder choice; a market map from public sources exists at low confidence. No demand data.

No fundraising target is set and no fundraising claim is made. Hospitality investors, strategic and brewery partners, angels and later debt are all possible; venture capital is not assumed.

Use of funds, by category

  • Legal / Ip: Name decision; trademark path; alcohol structure; formation
  • Product Validation: Repeated personal prototypes, supplier samples, small lawful tastings
  • Commercial Food Pilots: Commissary pop-up or residency data on mix, speed, cost
  • Brewing Pilots: Qualified brewer and pilot or collaboration batches
  • Brand Finalization: Final identity after the name decision
  • Architecture / Engineering: Real drawings against a real site
  • Site Diligence: Rent, NNN, grease, ventilation, drainage, parking, permits
  • Equipment: Kitchen and brewery equipment sized by evidence
  • Construction: Build-out
  • Working Capital: Cash until the unit is self-sustaining
  • Team: Executive chef, brewer, operations, finance as needed (see team-blueprint.csv)
  • Marketing / Launch: Public launch after gates
  • Contingency: Cost of being wrong on the above

No amounts are stated because none has been earned by evidence yet. There is no market-size claim, no projection, no customer, no sale, no quote and no professional opinion in this view.

The name

NASHA is the founder's internal working name. A same-name restaurant has been reported in Austin, so the name carries a legal question that must be reviewed by an attorney before any name-dependent spend. Nothing here claims clearance, ownership or exclusivity.

NASHA is a future Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas, in development.

The name was chosen by the founder. Legal clearance of the name is pending. Nothing here claims trademark ownership. There is no brewery, restaurant or truck open, and nothing is for sale. No site has been chosen.

In Hindi and Urdu, nasha means intoxication or addiction. We chose it for the feeling of being drawn in by food, craft and company. We take that meaning seriously and will never present excess or addiction as something to admire. Cultural advisors will review the name and our language before launch.

Images show a possible future. The photographic-style pictures are concept visualizations made with AI tools and edited, and the drawings are illustrations. They are not photographs of NASHA, of its food, or of its beer. About these images.

Menu items are designs for testing, not served food. Heat and vegetarian labels describe how a dish is designed, not a certified allergen or dietary statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. If you drink, drink responsibly. Alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age.

The word NASHA in the header and in some pictures is a temporary typographic placeholder, set in a standard font. It is not a logo, not an official brand mark, and no trademark is claimed. No logo has been approved or released.
